components.gap: Supply the historical chain stated by both sources: Durrett (p.152) attributes Theorem 3.4.14 to Levy as 'the last word on convergence to the normal distribution' and describes Gnedenko-Kolmogorov (1954) as containing the last word on many results about sums of independent random variables; Gnedenko-Kolmogorov (p.172) attribute Section 35, Theorem 1 to A. Ya. Khintchine [52], W. Feller [27] and P. Levy [75] (footnote), assert by their Section 33 that all stable laws and only these have non-empty domains of attraction, call the determination of these domains one of the fundamental problems of the theory of stable laws to which Section 35 gives the complete solution, and contrast the very wide class attracted by the normal law with the other stable domains. The chapter opening (parts 1-14) and def:p15-nda-historical-boundary (parts 301-312) state none of these; an unrouted treatment exists in this packet's owned file handbook/parts/p15/limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02c-p15-016.tex (not \input by handbook/parts/p15.tex, so not counted; its completeness is not assessed here) (sec:p15-w02c-p15-016-framing, def:p15-w02c-p15-016-boundary).
